source.title: Evaluate Facturapi as a transmission platform

labels.name: technical
labels.description: Not a feature, not a bug, it's technical

source.body:
Facturapi (`facturapi.io`) is a Mexican CFDI 4.0 API: it builds, signs and stamps invoices through a PAC, the SAT-authorized certification provider. Entry is 299 MXN per month plus 0.60 MXN per stamp.

The answer is no. Facturapi cannot take a document Invoicerr already built, nor a CFDI XML. `POST /v2/invoices` accepts a JSON object in its own model (`customer`, `items`, `payment_form`, `use`). The public OpenAPI 3.1 document lists 89 paths and 120 operations; none uploads a document for stamping. The only raw XML accepted is one complement node, `complements: [{ "type": "custom", "data": "<xml/>" }]`, "XML code of your complement".

The invoice is recreated in the platform's model, and Mexico has none of Factur-X, UBL or CII anyway.

## Context

A Mexican invoice is a CFDI, a SAT-owned schema stamped by a PAC. SAT states that CFDI 4.0 took effect on 1 January 2022 and that "desde el 1 de abril de 2023 es la única válida" (Anexo 20, consulted 2026-11-01).

Invoicerr has no Mexico support: `countries/data/` stops at `de`, `dz`, `fr`, `it`, `pl`, `pt`, no provider builds a CFDI, and `countries/mexico.md` says so. This is a country project, not a second channel for a format we emit.

Facturapi is not a PAC: onboarding requires the Carta Manifiesto, "que autoriza a nuestro PAC a timbrar facturas", and the status 202 guide names PADE as the party that stamps.

## Access and API

Reference at `docs.facturapi.io/api`, OpenAPI 3.1, base `https://www.facturapi.io/v2`, Bearer key per organization for test and live. "You do not need to pay for a subscription to use the API in the Test environment".

Webhooks are signed with seven events, including `invoice.status_updated` and `invoice.cancellation_status_updated`. Drafts stamp later, a PAC intermittency returns `202` and retries five times.

Two strings per company, but the company must also upload its CSD, the key that lets the PAC sign in its name, and sign the Carta Manifiesto before a live stamp.

## Formats accepted

Input is JSON only: types `I` income, `E` egress (the credit note), `P` payment, `N` payroll, `T` transfer. Complements are `pago`, `nomina`, `carta_porte` 3.1, `comercio_exterior` 2.0, `leyendas_fiscales` and `custom`. Output is CFDI 4.0 XML, PDF and ZIP.

No Factur-X, UBL or CII. The mapping lands on the caller: a SAT `product_key`, unit code and tax object per line, an RFC, tax regime and postal code per customer, a `payment_form` and a `use` per invoice. Invoicerr holds none of these catalogues.

## Statuses

`status` is `pending`, `valid`, `canceled`, `draft` or `failed`; `cancellation_status` is `none`, `verifying`, `pending`, `accepted`, `rejected` or `expired`, and `PUT /invoices/{id}/status` re-consults SAT. Cancelling is `DELETE /invoices/{id}?motive=01..04`, with `substitution` for 01 and 04. The receipt is downloadable, but "Facturapi can only retrieve receipts for requests submitted through its service. For cancellations performed externally, validate the current CFDI status using `verification_url`."

A real SAT read-back, but issuance only: no delivery status, no buyer acceptance, only the acceptance of a cancellation.

## Incoming reception

Reception is the Descarga Masiva product: 999 MXN per organization per month plus 0.20 MXN per synchronized CFDI, with the FIEL uploaded, since "The FIEL is required to use bulk CFDI downloads". It pulls issued and received CFDI from SAT, month by month.

The API exposes the record: `GET /invoices` filters on `issuer_type=receiving` and `sat_imported=true`, and `zip-requests` packages a month. Readable, not actionable: no endpoint starts a sync, no webhook fires on arrival.

## Real entry price

API 299 MXN per month plus 0.60 MXN per stamp, VAT included. Reception 999 MXN per organization per month plus 0.20 MXN per synchronized CFDI. Both for one organization: 1,298 MXN before consumption, about 61 EUR at the ECB rate of 21.1237 MXN/EUR on 2026-10-30.

## Effort: L

Not because the API is hard, because the payload does not exist yet.

Towards M: one POST of JSON, one PUT for the status, two credential strings, a small signed webhook contract. With a CFDI object in hand, the transport is an afternoon next to `iopole-transport.ts`.

Towards L, five reasons. No CFDI provider exists, so the semantic invoice must be mapped to SAT catalogues (product, unit, tax object, RFC, tax regime, postal code, `use`, `payment_form`, `export`). A credit note is not a UBL CreditNote but a CFDI type `E` with `related_documents` carrying the original UUID. A country file is needed, with the sections `adding-a-country.md` requires, all unresearched. The CSD, and for reception the FIEL, go to a third party: a security decision before a coding one. Two status axes, a recovery path, stampable drafts and a `verification_url` fallback map onto none of the current pollers.

The one thing that would move this to M is an endpoint taking a signed CFDI XML. It does not exist.

## What it unlocks

Mexico, with every CFDI type and the complements that matter there: payment, payroll, Carta Porte 3.1, foreign trade 2.0. Multi-RFC at no extra cost fits firms following several clients.

Nothing for the formats Invoicerr builds, and no PDP or Peppol access point: it is an issuer, and a receiver only through SAT's bulk download.

## Sources, consulted 2026-11-01

`docs.facturapi.io/api` and its OpenAPI 3.1 document (`/redocusaurus/api-en.yaml`); guides for invoices and cancellations; `facturapi.io/pricing`; `facturapi.io/descarga-masiva`; SAT Anexo 20, `omawww.sat.gob.mx/tramitesyservicios/Paginas/anexo_20.htm`; ECB rate for 2026-10-30; `dev` at `e70c603`.

## Not verified

- SAT's PAC register: `sat.gob.mx` answers 403 here, so "not a PAC" rests on Facturapi's wording.
- Whether the API can start a Descarga Masiva sync, or read the XML of a received CFDI.
- Latency of the SAT download, and test quotas.
- Whether an externally stamped CFDI can be registered by any other route.

comments.author: invoicerr-automation[bot]
comments.text:
Access and API, as read from the public OpenAPI document and the guides on 2026-11-01.

Documentation is public in Spanish and English. The reference at `docs.facturapi.io/api` is generated from an OpenAPI 3.1 document (title "Facturapi", version "2.0", server `https://www.facturapi.io/v2`, 89 paths, 120 operations, 13 tags). The raw document is served at `docs.facturapi.io/redocusaurus/api-en.yaml`, which is what the counts above come from. This corrects nothing in the inventory, which already said the API and sandbox are public.

Authentication is a Bearer secret key, and the key itself selects the environment and the organization. Three kinds exist: a Test key per organization (cannot update the organization configuration), a Live key per organization (can), and a User key for the account (creates organizations, users, roles and keys). Test and live are independent: "The resources created by an organization in one environment are inaccessible to other organizations or to the same organization in different environments." The concepts page is explicit that no subscription is needed for the test environment, and the pricing page also advertises a 14-day API trial without a card. A test invoice never reaches SAT and has no fiscal value.

For Invoicerr this has one design consequence worth flagging before any code: with superpdp and Iopole the environment comes from the channel row (`ResolvedChannelConfig.environment`) and the credentials are the same in both. Here the key is the environment. A company config must therefore hold either both keys with the environment choosing which one to use, or a single key plus a stored environment flag, and the connect form has to say which. Storing one key and toggling an environment flag would silently send live invoices from a test key, or the reverse.

Onboarding a company is four steps, all documented: create the organization, `PUT /organizations/{id}/legal` for the fiscal data, `PUT /organizations/{id}/certificate` for the CSD, then sign the Carta Manifiesto (dashboard, public portal, or an embeddable iframe without logos). Only then does a live stamp work. A User key can create an organization and mint its test and live keys through `/organizations/{id}/apikeys/test` and `/apikeys/live`, which is the shape a multi-tenant Invoicerr would need if it ever provisioned accounts on behalf of users.

Asynchronous behaviour is real and documented in two places. `async: true`, or any payload above 2 MB (around 5,000 items), returns the invoice with `status: pending` and null `stamp` and `uuid`. `POST /invoices/{id}/stamp` stamps an existing draft once `is_ready_to_stamp` is true; `PUT /invoices/{id}` edits a draft. A recognized PAC intermittency returns `202 Accepted` with the invoice kept as `pending`, the folio reserved for six hours, and five recovery attempts ten minutes apart, the first at minute 10, after which the invoice becomes `failed` and the folio is released. The guide's own instruction: "While the invoice remains pending, do not create it again or assign its folio to another document."

Rate limits are enforced by operation class and by authenticated identity, with IP-based limits for unauthenticated calls, and "We do not publish exact per-endpoint thresholds". The contract is `429` with a `Retry-After` header and the error code `rate_limit_exceeded`, the same policy in test and live. The guide asks for queues on writes, exponential backoff with jitter, and preservation of the `X-Facturapi-Log-Id` response header for correlation.

Pagination is `page` and `limit`, with `limit` capped at 100 and a hard ceiling of 3,000 results across pages (30 pages at the default). That is a real constraint for a backfill or a reconciliation sweep, and it is smaller than what the reception design would want.

Webhooks are created through the API and are signed. The `secret` is returned only when the webhook is created, the signature travels in the `Facturapi-Signature` header, and `POST /webhooks/validate-signature` takes `{secret, payload, signature}` and verifies the raw body. The seven events are `invoice.status_updated`, `invoice.cancellation_status_updated`, `invoice.created_from_dashboard`, `invoice.global_invoice_created`, `receipt.status_updated`, `receipt.self_invoice_complete` and `customer.edit_link_completed`. A wildcard `*` appears in responses but is refused in create and update requests.

Two smaller conveniences matter for an adapter. `external_id` stores our own document reference and is searchable (`GET /invoices?external_id=`), and `idempotency_key` prevents duplicates on retry, though Facturapi does not enforce uniqueness on `external_id`. Error messages follow `Accept-Language: en` or `es`, while "External SAT/PAC messages retain their original language", so a mapping layer cannot assume English text.

Official SDKs exist for Node.js (npm), C#, Java and PHP; anything else uses the REST API directly. The Backend is NestJS, so a typed client generated from the OpenAPI document would also be viable, but the SDKs are thin and the raw contract is small enough to hand-write, the same choice `iopole/iopole-client.ts` already makes.

comments.author: invoicerr-automation[bot]
comments.text:
Formats, statuses and reception, checked on 2026-11-01.

Formats, as the input model. `POST /v2/invoices` takes `InvoiceCreateInput`, a discriminated union on the invoice type, and the income branch requires `customer`, `items` and `payment_form`. A customer carries `legal_name`, `tax_id` (the RFC), `tax_system` (the SAT regime code) and `address.zip`; a line carries `quantity`, `product.description`, `product.product_key` (ClaveProdServ), `product.price`, `unit_key`, `unit_name` and `taxes` (`IVA`, `IEPS`, with rate or factor). Optional fields include `use` (c_UsoCFDI, default G03 and forced to S01 for foreign or generic RFCs), `payment_method` (PUE or PPD), `currency`, `exchange`, `conditions`, `related_documents`, `global` (periodicity, months, year, mandatory when the buyer is `XAXX010101000` public in general) and `export`. The invoice maximum is 5,000 items.

The five invoice types are `I` income, `E` egress, `P` payment, `N` payroll and `T` transfer. Retentions are a separate resource with their own create, stamp, copy, download and email endpoints. Complements are `pago`, `nomina`, `carta_porte` 3.1, `comercio_exterior` 2.0, `leyendas_fiscales` and `custom`.

The only XML ingress is `custom`. Its `data` field is "XML code of your complement as you want it to be inserted in the XML. It must contain only one root XML node", and the guide adds that the PDF needs the complement text added separately through `pdf_custom_section`. So a caller may inject a complement node, and nothing else. There is no request field anywhere in the contract that takes an invoice document, a file, a base64 payload or a URL to fetch.

What comes out is CFDI 4.0 XML, a PDF, a ZIP, and a cancellation receipt in XML or PDF, through `GET /invoices/{id}/xml`, `/pdf`, `/zip` or `/download-url/{format}` (a temporary URL that "grants access to that one file while it is valid"). No conversion to or from Factur-X, UBL, CII, XRechnung or FatturaPA exists, which is coherent: those are not Mexican formats, and Facturapi is not in the EN 16931 business at all.

The decisive point, restated with the fields. To send one invoice, Invoicerr would have to produce, per line, a SAT product key, a unit key, a tax object code and a tax breakdown, and per party an RFC, a tax regime and a postal code, plus a payment form and a use code for the document. Those are SAT catalogues, not neutral EN 16931 concepts. A mapping is possible, but it is a semantic translation with a rejected stamp as the failure mode, and it is the opposite of depositing bytes we already built. That is why the conclusion is evaluate and the effort is L.

Statuses. `status` has five values: `pending`, `valid`, `canceled`, `draft`, `failed`. `cancellation_status` has six: `none`, `verifying`, `pending`, `accepted`, `rejected`, `expired`. `PUT /invoices/{id}/status` "consults the status of a stamped invoice at the SAT and updates the invoice object", which is the polling path. Cancelling is `DELETE /invoices/{id}` with `motive` 01, 02, 03 or 04; 01 and 04 require `substitution` with the Facturapi id or the UUID of the replacing document. `pending` means the receiver must approve, `verifying` means SAT is validating, `accepted` moves the invoice to `status: canceled`.

The cancellation receipt has a limit that matters for a transport: "Facturapi can only retrieve receipts for requests submitted through its service. For cancellations performed externally, validate the current CFDI status using `verification_url`." So a company that cancels in the SAT portal leaves Facturapi with a stale view, and the only fallback is the public verification URL, which is per document and not a polling API.

There is no delivery status and no buyer acceptance. A CFDI is complete once stamped: the buyer receives the XML and PDF by email (`POST /invoices/{id}/email`) or downloads them, and no acknowledgement, no read receipt and no acceptance exists at document level. The only receiver-side signal in the whole contract is the acceptance or rejection of a cancellation, which is a correction event, not a delivery event. Any conformity poller built on Facturapi would have exactly two states worth storing: stamped and valid, and cancelled or not.

Reception. It exists, but as a batch pull from the authority, not as a channel that receives documents. The Descarga Masiva product is 999 MXN per organization per month plus 0.20 MXN per synchronized CFDI, and it requires the FIEL: "Uploads the organization's e.firma (FIEL) files. The e.firma (FIEL) is not required to create CFDI. To stamp CFDI, you only need to upload the Digital Seal Certificate (CSD). The FIEL is required to use bulk CFDI downloads." The product page adds that it downloads issued and received CFDI for the organization's RFC, month by month, that the current month can sync automatically, and that it generates a PDF for each downloaded XML.

The API side is read only. `GET /invoices` filters on `issuer_type=receiving` and `sat_imported=true`, both documented ("Indicates whether the invoice was issued by your organization or received from a third party", and "true for CFDIs imported from SAT"). `POST /invoices/zip-requests` packages a year and month with `issuer_type`, `sat_imported` and the invoice types, and returns a ZIP. No endpoint starts, schedules or accelerates a sync, and none of the seven webhook events concerns a received invoice. A reception poller would therefore have to list received invoices on a date window and deduplicate on UUID, with a latency that is not documented anywhere.

One asymmetry to note for a future design: the Descarga Masiva page says issued CFDI obtained that way can be cancelled and their cancellation status consulted. It says nothing equivalent for received ones, and the API offers no accept or reject action on them. Reception through Facturapi is for visibility and reconciliation, not for a business workflow that answers the supplier.

comments.author: invoicerr-automation[bot]
comments.text:
Price, effort and value.

Price, read from `facturapi.io/pricing` on 2026-11-01, all figures VAT included and in Mexican pesos.

| Product | Subscription | Consumption |
|---|---|---|
| CFDI API | 299 MXN per month | 0.60 MXN per stamp |
| Web invoicing | 199 MXN per organization per month | 0.60 MXN per stamp |
| E-Receipts and self-invoicing | 599 MXN per organization per month | 0.40 MXN per receipt, 0.60 MXN per stamp |
| Descarga Masiva (SAT bulk download) | 999 MXN per organization per month | 0.20 MXN per synchronized CFDI |
| Stripe app | 299 MXN per organization per month | 0.60 MXN per stamp |
| Additional team user | 99 MXN per user per month | none |

The API includes two users per organization and is multi-RFC at no extra cost per RFC; the other products are sold per organization, which here means per RFC. Billing is immediate for the subscription and deferred for consumption: stamps and synchronized documents are added to the next monthly invoice. Volume pricing exists but needs a sales conversation. No setup fee, no minimum volume, no annual commitment and no activation delay are published, which is the opposite of the Pagero situation and the strongest part of this file.

For Invoicerr the realistic line is 299 MXN for emission plus 999 MXN for reception, so 1,298 MXN per organization per month before consumption, about 61 EUR at the ECB reference rate of 21.1237 MXN/EUR on 2026-10-30. At 100 stamps a month the API line is 359 MXN, about 3.6 MXN per invoice; at 1,000 stamps it is 899 MXN. The subscription dominates at every volume a small issuer reaches, so the per-document price is not the deciding cost. The test environment is free and needs no subscription, which means the integration can be built and demonstrated before any payment.

Effort: L, and the body's five reasons are the short version. Concretely, what would have to exist before a single live invoice leaves:

1. A CFDI mapping layer, either a new provider in `formats/` or a dedicated mapper in the transport. It needs the SAT catalogues that this repository does not carry: ClaveProdServ, ClaveUnidad, c_FormaPago, c_MetodoPago, c_UsoCFDI, c_RegimenFiscal, c_ObjetoImp, and the IVA and IEPS rate tables. That is data sourcing with a legal edge, the same class of work as `vat-rates/` and `country-identifiers/`, but with SAT as the only authority.
2. `countries/data/mx.json`, with the sections `adding-a-country.md` requires. Today the country directory stops at six countries and the Mexico page is a warning, not a file. Every section would be a new research task with its own primary sources.
3. A credit-note path. A CFDI credit note is a type `E` document with `related_documents` pointing at the original UUID, not a UBL CreditNote. `deliversCreditNotes` would have to be true only if that rewrite is honest, otherwise the transport must refuse by name.
4. `transports/facturapi-transport.ts` plus a client, with two credential strings and the environment stored explicitly, because the key itself selects test or live. This is the small part: one POST, one poller shaped like `pdp-status-poller.ts`, and a webhook receiver for `invoice.status_updated` and `invoice.cancellation_status_updated` to avoid polling every pending invoice.
5. Optionally a reception poller, behind the Descarga Masiva product, which brings the FIEL into scope. That is a separate decision about holding a taxpayer's private key and password, and it deserves its own security review rather than being folded into a transport PR.

That is three or four separable pull requests, not one, and the first two are country work rather than channel work. Nothing here is a `baseUrl` entry in `pdp`.

What contradicts the inventory lead. The 299 MXN per month is confirmed, and so is 0.60 MXN per stamp. The public API and a usable sandbox are confirmed, and the sandbox is free, which the lead did not say. "PAC mexicain CFDI 4.0" is right in substance but imprecise: Facturapi is not the PAC, it is the API above one, and its own documentation says the Carta Manifiesto authorizes "our PAC" and names PADE as the stamping party. "Effort S" is contradicted: with no CFDI provider, no country file and no credit-note model, this is L by the repository's own definitions. "Score 3/3" only holds if the score measures documentation, price transparency and sandbox access; it does not measure integration friction, and on that axis Facturapi is the most expensive kind of cheap platform, because the cheap part is the API and the expensive part is the invoice model Invoicerr does not have.

Value, honestly stated. Mexico is a real market that Invoicerr does not serve, and Facturapi is the lowest-friction way to reach it that this research has found: transparent price, free sandbox, multi-RFC, and a genuinely good SAT status read-back with the four legal cancellation motives. But it unlocks nothing for Factur-X, UBL, CII or Peppol, and it is not a transmission platform in the sense the other issues in this milestone use the word. It is an issuer with a cheap API, and the work it needs is a Mexico country project.

Recommendation: do not open an adapter now. If Mexico becomes a target, sequence the country file and the CFDI mapping first, prove one stamped invoice against the free test environment, and only then write the transport. The one question worth asking Facturapi support before any of that: is there an endpoint, documented or private, that accepts a CFDI XML already signed with the company's CSD for stamping. If the answer is yes, this file changes and the effort drops to M.
